title: Shard alignment trace and quick debugging playbook
body:
Context:
- Temp scratchpad for the incident where a model that previously loaded (v0.9 ckpt) fails after we re-sharded/packed for A100 pool. Seen downstream as: inference process crashes on first forward with storage size mismatch.
- Model: customer-bert-xl (internal name), original checkpoint produced by export pipeline (2024-06). Resharding step: split into 8 shards, compressed into tar.gz, uploaded to GCS, then streamed into serving hosts.
- Symptoms: some hosts load fine, others error immediately. Non-deterministic across identical instance types.

Timeline and commands tried (chronological):
- 2024-09-26 09:14 - Initial reproduce on dev-1 (a100-small)
  command: python3 -c "import torch; torch.load('shard-000.pt', map_location='cpu')"
  result: RuntimeError: Storage size mismatch for tensor 'transformer.wte.weight': expected 3019898880, got 3019898872
  note: byte delta of 8 — suggests truncated/extra bytes in shard file.

- 2024-09-26 09:22 - Quick check on GCS copy
  command: gsutil ls -l gs://model-buckets/customer-bert-xl/reshard-20240925/
  output: listed eight shard files with sizes: shard-000.pt (1203456), shard-001.pt (1203456), ... shard-007.pt (1203448)  --> shard-007 is 8 bytes smaller.

- 2024-09-26 09:30 - Re-download using gsutil with md5/sha256 check
  command: gsutil cp gs://.../shard-007.pt ./ && sha256sum shard-007.pt && gsutil hash gs://.../shard-007.pt
  result: local sha256 != GCS hash (GCS reports different hash).
  hypothesis: upload truncated or GCS stream consistency issue during upload.

- 2024-09-26 09:45 - Inspect tarball (we had an alternate pipeline that uploaded a tar.gz containing shards)
  command: tar -tzf reshard-20240925.tar.gz | sed -n '1,40p'
  result: all shard entries present. Extract specific shard via: tar -xOzf reshard-20240925.tar.gz shards/shard-007.pt > /tmp/s07.pt && sha256sum /tmp/s07.pt
  note: sha256 of extracted file matched expectation in CI snapshot but not the GCS object.

- 2024-09-26 10:05 - Quick hexdump around end of file to see truncation pattern
  command: tail -c 64 /tmp/s07.pt | hexdump -C
  output: ... last 8 bytes: 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
  compare: GCS copy last bytes: 4d 5a 1f 8b 00 00 00 00 -> suggests corruption/extra header bytes from gzip?

- 2024-09-26 10:30 - Attempt load with non-strict key loading to see if tensor names are fine
  command: python3 - <<'PY'
import torch
sd = torch.load('/tmp/s07.pt', map_location='cpu')
print(list(sd.keys())[:12])
print(sd['transformer.wte.weight'].numel())
PY
  output: Key list sane, but accessing .numel() raises exception (storage size mismatch).

- 2024-09-26 11:00 - Cross-compare shard index mapping (index.json) vs actual file sizes
  command: jq . index.json
  observation: index lists byte ranges assuming concatenated tar entries; suspected off-by-one when we used streaming uploader that used chunked writes.

Diagnostic script (quick python to detect off-by-N across shards):
  python3 - <<'PY'
import os
sizes = {f: os.path.getsize(f) for f in sorted(os.listdir('.')) if f.startswith('shard-')}
for k,v in sizes.items():
    print(k, v, v % 4096)
PY
Result: two shards return size % 4096 == 8 (i.e., misaligned to 4k pages).

Error snippets captured: (copied raw)
- RuntimeError: Storage size mismatch for tensor 'lm_head.weight': expected 1509949440, got 1509949432
- safetensors.errors.SafetensorError: header size mismatch: claimed 12345 bytes but only 12337 present
- EOFError: Compressed file ended before the end-of-stream marker
- tar: Unexpected EOF in archive

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Upload/streaming corruption: pipeline used resumable upload with a buggy chunk size that caused last chunk to be 8 bytes short for some files. GCS object stored truncated file. (High likelihood; matches different GCS hash vs tar-extracted copy.)
2) Mis-ordered shard index / lexicographic sort mismatch: resharder wrote logical shard order but uploader sorted filenames lexicographically resulting in wrong concatenation for index-based loader. (Medium)\3) Platform-specific IO buffer issue on older kernel/driver causing atomic writes to be split wrongly under high concurrency (Low)\4) Endianness/metadata header mismatch between safetensors vs torch ckpt (Low if using .pt, higher if using safetensors).

Mitigations tried and outcomes:
- Re-run uploader with --no-resume chunked set to 8M and set Content-MD5. Outcome: new files uploaded and sha256 matches local, hosts can load. (Good temporary fix.)
- Re-extracted tarball and uploaded shards individually rather than streaming tar. Outcome: loads reliably.
- Quick conversion to safetensors to see if loader is more tolerant: safetensors wrote file fine but failed during conversion because original file truncated. (No win.)
- Implemented post-upload verification step in CI: compute sha256 locally and verify GCS object in pipeline before promoting. (Deployed to staging.)

Notes to self / actionable next steps:
- Add a small script to uploader to double-check size and sha256 after upload; if mismatch, re-upload and alert. Put this as a required check in reshard CI job.
- Root cause triage: check the uploader logs (resumable session ids) for the affected timestamps (see linked JIRA). The truncated uploads correlate with high-concurrency window in our uploader service.
- For immediate customer mitigation: re-run reshard pipeline and push verified shards to their project; coordinate with CS to schedule short maintenance window.
- Add unit test to re-sharder that simulates chunked upload and validates last-chunk size handling.

Quick heuristics for future debugging (copy into runbook):
- If torch.load throws Storage size mismatch: compare local size vs remote size; hexdump last 64 bytes; check for tar/gzip signatures (1f 8b).
- If only some hosts fail: check if they fetched different shard object (compare sha256 on host to canonical).
- If safetensors header error: run hexdump and check for two appended gzip headers (duplication from double-compression).

Random notes + small snippets I saved:
- awk to find files with size mismatch across buckets: gsutil ls -l gs://bucket/** | awk '{print $1, $2}' | sort -k2n | uniq -c
- quick python to reassemble shards in correct order using index.json: (in repo snippets)
- Slack convo: #infra-uploader where @riley called out flaky resumable token handling around 09/25 (see JIRA-1887).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why did only 2 shards show 8-byte delta? Are these always the last shards in the logical model order? Might point to a pattern in how we flush the last buffer of the per-shard writer.
- Is there any OS-level difference between hosts that succeeded vs failed? (kernel, glibc, mount options) — schedule side-by-side compare.

TL;DR: Likely upload-truncation / chunk handling bug in the reshard uploader. Immediate fix: push verified re-uploaded shards; longer-term: strict post-upload verification + uploader unit tests.

-- Harper
